In the New Testament, Matias is known as one of the twelve apostles and an author of the Gospel of Matthew. This name has a rich history and continues to be popular among Christians today. The name Matias is derived from the Hebrew name Mattathias, meaning 'gift of God'. It is also related to the Hebrew name Mattityahu, which is the origin of the name Matthew. The name Matias has a strong religious significance and is often given to boys in honor of the apostle and evangelist.
